items.question: List<T> versus array versus Dictionary — how do you choose?
items.answer: Array when the length is known and will not change (a decoded SQS batch you will not grow). List<T> when you append. Dictionary when the operation is lookup by key (Redis-style cache, auth tenant map). HashSet when the question is membership. Queue when order is FIFO and you drain from the front.
followUps: Why is List<T> not a concurrent structure?
When would you use ImmutableArray instead?
items.sixtySeconds: Array = fixed. List = grow. Dictionary = key. HashSet = unique. Queue = FIFO. None of them replace Channel for multi-producer work.

items.question: What does foreach actually call?
items.answer: It obtains an enumerator via GetEnumerator (instance or extension), then loops on MoveNext and Current. Types need not implement IEnumerable if they have the right pattern. A null collection throws NullReferenceException. await foreach is the IAsyncEnumerable path — module 13.
followUps: What happens if you mutate a List while foreach is running?
Why can foreach use a struct enumerator?
items.sixtySeconds: foreach is MoveNext/Current. Null throws. Mutation of List invalidates the enumerator. Async version is later.

items.question: Why can yield return surprise you in a CSV importer?
items.answer: The method returns immediately with an iterator object. The file is not read until foreach. A second foreach opens the file again. Exceptions surface at MoveNext, not at the call. If you need a snapshot, call ToList once.
followUps: Can you mix yield return and return in the same method?
items.sixtySeconds: yield is deferred. Two enumerations, two passes. ToList to materialize. Do not hold a live SqlDataReader across both.

items.question: Are collection expressions lazy like LINQ?
items.answer: No. Microsoft documents that a collection expression always creates a collection holding every element, even if the target type is IEnumerable<T>. Use them for literals and spreads, not for infinite sequences.
items.sixtySeconds: C# 12. Eager. Can target arrays, List, Span, interfaces. Not a LINQ query.
